messages:
maria: quick note from support: people save console views with model filters but then get confused when runtime routes to a cheaper model. we should clarify what a saved view actually guarantees
lucas: can you show an example payload? our current saved-view object is just {filters, name, scope, owner}
sam: yep. end result: user saves a view with model: 'redwood-3b' but when invoked the routing policy swapped to 'rdw-3b-quant' for cost -> customer filed a ticket
maria: proposal: add explicit routing intent at save time. minimal UX: small line in save modal: "Routing: [ ] Allow runtime fallback  [ ] Pin model (no fallback)" plus an info icon with cost/SLA blurb
ana: ana here. API options: (A) pinned_model_id string, (B) routing_intent: "pin"|"prefer"|"any". I prefer pinned_model_id because it's unambiguous. if pinned_model_id present runtime must treat it as a hard constraint
kevin: agree on pinned_model_id. if the model isn't available we should return a 409 with a clear message rather than silently using fallback. silent remapping is the pain point
lucas: implementation note: server should store: saved_view.{filters, pinned_model_id?, routing_metadata:{estimated_tokens, sample_ts}} — but telemetry objects must be flattened for export/joining. we'll add tags: saved_view_id, pinned_model_id, routing_intent to telemetry events
maria: UX: show a badge next to saved views in the list: "Pinned model" (hover shows model & region availability) or "Routable" (hover shows typical fallback list + cost delta). show estimated token burn under name (rounded)
sam: where do we get the estimate? telemetry service can sample recent requests for the route+model combo and return median tokens/latency + 90% CI. lucas/eng-telemetry can add an endpoint: GET /telemetry/estimate?saved_view_id=xxx
lucas: yes we can. sample output as string in save modal: "Estimated tokens: ~1.3k (±300), median latency 220ms". also include note: "Estimate may vary by prompt length and routing policy"
ana: search/export: exported saved-views CSV/json must include pinned_model_id and estimated_tokens_sample. otherwise billing teams can't attribute costs correctly
kevin: rollout plan: feature-flag per-org, default behavior depends on org tier: self-serve => default "routable"; enterprise/dedicated => default "pinned" in console save modal. product to confirm final defaults
maria: deployment/canary: enable for 5% orgs, telemetry toggle that logs pin usage. devx-bot: feature flag created: feature/save-routing-intent - default off - created by devx-bot
sam: edge case: what if a pinned model is available in some regions but not the user's current region? runtime should reject at call time with a clear error and a suggested fallback list. console can prompt user to unpin or choose fallback
lucas: server contract change: POST /saved-views -> accepts optional "pinned_model_id". GET /saved-views returns pinned_model_id or null and also estimated_tokens string. we'll bump API minor version and keep backward compatible fallback for older clients
maria: copy for modal: "Pin a model to guarantee consistent outputs. Pinning prevents automatic fallback and may increase cost or latency. If the model is unavailable, requests will be rejected."
kevin: agree. ops: add alert when many clients start getting rejects due to unavailable pins, so we can reach out to customers before escalation
ana: tiny perf ask: don't make the save-blocking on telemetry estimate. fetch estimate asynchronously and show "estimating..." in the modal if not ready
maria: ok i'll draft the design PR with modal mock + API proto and link it here. thanks all :thumbsup:
